page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, delivering 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and features a large 480 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It includes 5669 GB of local NVMe storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier rating in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and single-threaded gzip compression both reached top-tier performance levels. Memory bandwidth tests showed top-tier speeds for small cached blocks at 7496.51 GB/sec, alongside strong uncached read and write speeds for large blocks. In database operations, the instance demonstrated top-tier performance, processing 159.97 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and scoring highly in Passmark database operations. Large language model inference benchmarks for prompt processing also fell into the top-tier category for both small and medium models.

The E96ds_v7 offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with high-speed local storage and advanced CPU instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. This hardware profile provides high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound and database-heavy workloads, as it reduces the need to scale horizontally. However, a notable tradeoff is the average single-core CPU performance and average Passmark memory score, indicating that workloads relying heavily on single-threaded execution may not fully exploit the system's capabilities. This server is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and data-intensive ETL processes.
